# Surgical Outcomes

This folder contains specific clinical quality indicators used within the Danish Acute Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) to measure surgical timeliness and postoperative mortality. The indicators track critical performance metrics such as the proportion of patients receiving a CT scan within two hours of arrival, time-to-surgery for severe conditions like perforation, ischemia, or ileus, and 30-day postoperative mortality stratified by the patient's Charlson Comorbidity Index score. Each page details the indicator's definition, national and regional performance against development targets, and supplementary mortality analyses, providing a comprehensive, risk-adjusted view of acute surgical care quality across Danish hospitals.

## Pages

- [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] — Tracks the proportion of patients receiving a CT scan within 120 minutes of hospital arrival, noting that national performance remains far below the 90% development target.
- [[indikator-4x|Indikator 4x]] — Measures the percentage of patients with perforation, ischemia, or bleeding who undergo surgery within six hours of arrival, alongside supplementary 30- and 90-day mortality statistics.
- [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]] — Evaluates the timeliness of surgical intervention for ileus patients without ischemia or perforation, targeting operations within 24 hours and reporting associated mortality outcomes.
- [[indikator-9b|Indikator 9b]] — A supplementary metric detailing 30-day postoperative mortality for acute surgery patients with a moderate comorbidity burden (Charlson Score of 1 or 2).
- [[indikator-9c|Indikator 9c]] — A supplementary metric analyzing 30-day postoperative mortality for acute surgery patients with a high comorbidity burden (Charlson Score ≥ 3).
- [[indikator-10b|Indikator 10b]] — Assesses 30-day postoperative mortality among acute surgery patients with a Charlson Comorbidity Index score of 1 or 2 to provide risk-adjusted outcome comparisons.
- [[indikator-10c|Indikator 10c]] — Focuses on 30-day postoperative mortality for acute surgery patients with a high comorbidity risk (Charlson Score ≥ 3), ensuring fair performance evaluations across regions and hospitals.
